standard_prerequisites.name: Filtered colimits of abelian sheaves and the commutation of cohomology with such colimits on the objects of B
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the criterion for cohomology to commute with filtered colimits, which is exactly the hypothesis on the set B in the statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the reduction from the sheaf statement to the pointwise one.

core_obligations: Reduce to the objects of B (proof lines 2834-2845): since every object of the target site has a covering by elements of B, it suffices to check the identification of the sheaves on those objects.

Use the hypothesis (proof lines 2845-2852): on an object V of B the hypothesis identifies the cohomology of the colimit with the colimit of the cohomologies, which gives the identification of the higher direct images after sheafification.
proof_roadmap: Reduce the identification of the higher direct images to the objects of B.
Apply the hypothesis that cohomology commutes with the filtered colimit on those objects.
Conclude the identification of the sheaves.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the higher direct images of a filtered colimit of abelian sheaves along a morphism of sites are the colimits of the higher direct images, provided the commutation is known on a family of objects covering every object of the target site (statement lines 2821-2832). The proof reduces the sheaf-theoretic statement to a pointwise one over the objects in B (proof lines 2834-2845) and then applies the hypothesis there (proof lines 2845-2852). The non-formal content is the reduction of a statement about sheaves to a statement about their values on a covering family. The claim is H2: one reduction plus one application of the hypothesis.
